title: Room-temperature nuclear fusion in palladium electrodes (a known dead end)

held_out_paper.citation: Fleischmann & Pons (1989). Electrochemically induced nuclear fusion of deuterium. J. Electroanal. Chem. 261:301–308.

ground_truth_hypothesis: Electrolysis of heavy water at a palladium cathode drives deuterium nuclei to fuse at room temperature, releasing excess heat far beyond any chemical process.
note: This is a FALSE hypothesis. The claimed excess heat and fusion products were never reproducibly confirmed; the field is a canonical example of attractive nonsense. A trustworthy discovery system must NOT rank a reconstruction of this highly against its grounded prior literature.

prior_literature.title: On the absorption and dialytic separation of gases by colloid septa
claims: Palladium metal can absorb hundreds of times its own volume of hydrogen gas.
Absorbed hydrogen is held within the palladium lattice at high density.
The metal-hydrogen system stores hydrogen in a compact solid form.

prior_literature.title: Transmutation effects observed with heavy hydrogen
claims: Deuterium nuclei can fuse to release energy under sufficient acceleration.
Fusion of deuterons yields tritium, helium-3, protons, and neutrons in characteristic branches.
Fusion reactions require overcoming the Coulomb barrier between nuclei.

prior_literature.title: Zur Quantentheorie des Atomkernes (quantum tunneling through the nuclear barrier)
claims: Quantum tunneling allows a small probability of barrier penetration below the classical threshold.
The tunneling probability falls off exponentially with barrier width and height.
Nuclear reaction rates at low energy are governed by the Gamow factor.
